files.file: Services._upstream_lock serializes upstream subscribe/unsubscribe in _up_subscribe, _up_unsubscribe (also skips if ref_count>0) and watch_symbol; _configure_logging() (idempotent, INFO on "app", handler only if app and root have none) called from create_app.

ALERT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3.0 and ALERT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS=1.0; _drain_alerts (queue.join under wait_for) called first in close(); alert writer does task_done in finally and sleeps the backoff after a failed batch.

Appended 13 tests: race (2), concurrent watch_symbol, lock not wedged by failure, drain, bounded drain, close edge cases, backoff, no sleep on success, close during backoff, logging idempotence, rule-fired INFO record.

tests.test: Race test test_rule_created_while_last_browser_unsubscribe_in_flight (and the re-subscribe variant) FAILED on pre-fix main.py: "assert set() == {'AAPL'}" (final upstream state empty; unsubscribe landed last). Both PASS after the fix.
pytest offline from backend/: 70 passed, 15 skipped. With TEST_DATABASE_URL on a throwaway PG17 cluster (port 55432): 85 passed, 0 skipped. Cluster stopped and deleted.

commands_run.command: python -m pytest (offline and with TEST_DATABASE_URL); initdb/pg_ctl start/stop for throwaway cluster in %TEMP%

design_decisions.decision: Added lock-free fast paths (watch_symbol returns if ref_count>0; _up_subscribe returns if watched) before taking the lock, re-checked inside it. Spec said take the lock unconditionally; that deadlocked two existing tests that await inline while another task holds the lock inside a blocked upstream subscribe. Rejected: unconditional lock.
Drain uses queue.join() with task_done in the writer's finally, rather than polling empty(), so an in-flight batch is awaited.
Backoff sleep sits outside the per-batch try, so it is cancellable and close() cancels it right after the drain (drain completes before backoff starts since task_done runs first).

implementation.deviations: Fast paths above (minor). Mid-task I accidentally clobbered part of db.py with a bad string replace; I rebuilt it from HEAD plus the db.py hunk of iteration-2-baseline/tracked.diff (read only, in a temp dir) and reapplied the edits; a diff confirmed the only differences from the baseline db.py are the intended changes. No git state-changing commands were used. fake_db.py unchanged.
implementation.self_critique: The re-check in _up_unsubscribe relies on ref_count read without the manager lock; fine since the manager lock is already held by the caller. The failure-before evidence was taken on the pre-fix main.py before I edited it, not re-run on a separate copy afterwards. Logging handler test depends on global logger state.
